message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin (1889)**. **Why it’s so famous** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin – a leading figure of French sculpture who bridged Romanticism and modernism. | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast). Rodin began the work in the 1880s; the piece was completed and exhibited in 1889. | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist influence – dynamic, textured surfaces, and a focus on human emotion. | | **Iconic Elements** | The intimate embrace of a man and woman, the dramatic contrast between the rough, almost unfinished male torso and the smooth, idealized female form. | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Inspired countless reproductions, parodies, and homages worldwide.
• Its imagery has been used in advertising, film, and popular culture. | | **Legacy** | • Considered a milestone in modern sculpture, influencing subsequent generations of artists.
• Continues to be displayed in major museums (e.g., Musée Rodin in Paris, the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York). | **Other notable 19th‑century masterpieces** - **“The Thinker” (Le Penseur)** – Rodin, begun in 1880, first cast in 1902. Though its final casting is early 20th, the work’s conception and early models belong to the late 19th century. - **“The Gates of Hell” (Les Portes de l’Enfer)** – Rodin, 1880–1908, an ambitious monumental project inspired by Dante’s *Divine Comedy*. - **“The Birth of Venus” (La Naissance de Vénus)** – Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot, 1865, a reinterpretation of Botticelli’s classic. **Bottom line** While several works from the 19th century have achieved lasting fame, **Rodin’s “The Kiss” stands out as the most iconic and widely recognized sculpture of that era**.
